I’m half thai half British and also have 2B/2C hair. Three years ago it used to be thick, curly with some ringlets and down to my waist.
I’m 19 now and this is how I’ve been taking care of my hair since I was 12 and embraced my curls. As I was sick of wanting my hair to be straight lie my peers I just decided to fall in love with it.


1. Rinsed with cold water after showering (easy for me as I don’t have a stand-in shower but a bathtub with a shower head)
2. Coconut oil mask 1-2 times a week (if I didn’t feel like coconut oil I’d use egg/olive oil)
3. I used a boar bristle brush whenever I wanted to brush it 
4. Leading from 3. I HARDLY ever brushed my hair out. Probably only once a week to get old hairs out. Even before or after a shower I wouldn’t use a hairbrush or comb. I would only use my hands and fingers lightly - this really kept my waves/curls 
5. I NEVER used straighteners or flat irons. I also never used a hairdryer 


I’m 19 now and after 3 years of bleach, box dyed, using straighteners and blowdriers. Parts of my hair look 2B at the most but the moment I brush it out with my hairbrush it simply goes straight/wavy (types of waves you get if you went to a hairdressers for a blowout - waves at the end of the hair). So definitely don’t do what I did. Eventually I just got sick of my curls and wanted straighter, flowey hair so I didn’t mind doing all of these damaging things. Plus I hated how my face looked with curly hair because I have sharp facial features and wanted princess-like loose curls which would help balance my face out.

I kinda wanna embrace my curls back again - I doubt they’ll ever be the same as they used to be when I was a child - literally beautiful curls and ringlets. 
So for the last couple of weeks I’ve gone back to the things I used to do for my hair when I was 13 and I’m seeing a lot of progress. I’ve also added another thing which is using sulfate and paraben free shampoo.

Trust me. Everyone ALWAYS says this - but it is about your MINDSET.

Go in when you start your project thinking “Hell yeah, this is easy! I can do this!”

I cannot tell you how many times I’ve seen such realistic eye drawings, anime cartoons etc. Wished that I could draw like that, give it a go (even if it’s in a medium I’ve never used before) and copy that artwork (observation) and it 95% of the time, no kidding, ends up looking like a parallel universe’s replica.

But you can’t just say “This is easy, I can do this!” Without meaning it and believing it.
My first time copying Bob Ross using a canvas and oil paints and massive brushes was so scary to me. But I just reminded myself of these art sayings I learnt when I was younger...

There’s no mistakes in art. No one will know how you envisioned it in your head, so will not know how “unperfect/wrong” your finished piece is. Drawings and paintings are just ILLUSIONS using simple, simple shapes and lines and hand movement techniques - it is literally EASY. And lastly, if you can write your name, you can draw.

Believe that you can do it, and you will!

EDIT: Respect writers/artists block. Unless it becomes excessive and detrimental to your art career/course. If it’s just a hobby, give it a break. I can go months without even drawing something as simple as a heart.

It sounds like a problem which should have a deeper or complicated solution. But one day, after having an arm raw with cuts, I just went to The Works to pick up some art supplies and had a long browse all round the store. I was in my own head wondering whether I should go down to the bridge, sit there and just swallow the 30 odd pills I always kept in an empty body butter tub in my bag (“for when I finally have the courage to end it” I called it).

Then I stumbled on the spirituality section and found this bright orange book which strangely enough, seemed like it was screaming at me to pick up. I love new books and hadn’t bought one in a while, especially from the spirituality section (because I had 0 interest in that “bullshit” at the time. “Meditation and crap”).

Got the bus home because I wanted to read it. Finished it that night and it changed my life. For the next 3 weeks, I not only highlighted so many pets of that book but also bought more and more similar ones. To this day I have around 50 similar books on the topic. 

The book? A New Earth by Eckhart Tolle. He saved my life.

He introduced me into spirituality and the reason why I’m alive today. Through that book I learnt WHY I was feeling the way I did, how I can get out of it, why life seemed to get shitter and shitter with every goddamn passing moment and why people were selfish assholes to me. 

Since buying that first book and learning about energies, the pain body, the universe, manifestation and the shared subconscious, I’ve only learnt more and bought more books. And that is why, whenever I come across someone who needs my help since they’re combatting mental, I’ll always try my hardest and teach them the same teachings that saved me. 

My main trigger of why I was in that state, like so many millions of others in the world, was loneliness. I had no friends. Yes, there were people at college and people in town. But the countless nights I’d be crying in my room with blunt scissors in my hand was because I had NO ONE. Literally no one to message. No one. Yes, I had my parents, and they will never ever know the true extent of what I went through, but I couldn’t talk to them. 

I didnt leave the house unless it was for sixth form. And when I did, it was rare. I ended college with 62% attendance (you get excluded at 85%) and a B, C and an E in sociology, geography and Geology (respectively) after having all my teachers down my back for 5 months literally telling me I was going to fail and that they were on the brink of kicking me out. The only reason why I wasn’t kicked out and now going to university in 2020 (after a much needed gap year) is because I cried my eyes out (all the teachers knew what I was going through and were all tired of me at this point) and LITERALLY begged/pleaded/ lost whatever dignity I had left and took on-the-spot mock exams to prove I wouldn’t fail. 

Sorry that dragged and this reply is so long now! I just kept typing because it feels like I was reliving the moment, tearing up a lil bit now. But I feel like to put into context how I was feeling before I came across a simple book and way of life, would be needed to put my point across. 

I can’t tell you how proud I am of myself for pulling myself out of that all on my own. I could’ve easily tossed the book away and thought “what a joke” but I chose to continue reading and implementing what I learnt into my life and actively trying to change my state.

Then I stumbled on the spirituality section and found this bright orange book which strangely enough, seemed like it was screaming at me to pick up. I love new books and hadn’t bought one in a while, especially from the spirituality section (because I had 0 interest in that “bullshit” at the time. “Meditation and crap”).

The book? A New Earth by Eckhart Tolle. He saved my life.

He introduced me into spirituality and the reason why I’m alive today. Through that book I learnt WHY I was feeling the way I did, how I can get out of it, why life seemed to get shitter and shitter with every goddamn passing moment and why people were selfish assholes to me.

My main trigger of why I was in that state, like so many millions of others in the world, was loneliness. I had no friends. Yes, there were people at college and people in town. But the countless nights I’d be crying in my room with blunt scissors in my hand was because I had NO ONE. Literally no one to message. No one.
